title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and executed a paired experiment to test whether inserting an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial generation policy on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), every produced candidate was accepted by the verifier in both conditions (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We publish the full preregistration and execution bundle (responses, call traces, scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose why the ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates), and give artifact-grounded prescriptions (independent generation, adversarial temporal invariants, multi-verifier matrices, canary reachability tests, multi-model comparisons) for future verifier evaluations designed to produce informative discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Mapping operator intent (natural language) to low-level device configuration is central to modern NetOps. A common operational architecture is generation (LLM) → deterministic verifier → enact/rollback. We asked: does inserting an automated verifier that blocks verifier-detected violations reduce unsafe enactments versus an LLM-only pipeline? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and executed the run end-to-end, preserving model calls, responses, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and full SHA256 manifests. The run produced a deterministic ceiling: identical, verifier-accepted candidates in both pipelines for all 150 tasks (n11=150). This paper (1) reports the exact preregistered design and execution artifacts; (2) reports exact quantitative outcomes and preregistered inferential results (artifact-backed); and (3) gives an artifact-grounded diagnosis and concrete design prescriptions for future informative evaluations.
sections.related_work: We position this study among work on verifier-assisted NetOps pipelines, intent→configuration translation, and generate–validate–repair designs. Representative verified sources guiding our design include Aether (agentic AI + digital twin for validation) and recent surveys advocating workflow-centred evaluation for agentic NetOps (cited_record_ids). Research on constraint-based adaptation and generate–validate–repair loops (e.g., MeshAgent) motivated the paired design and the verifier-block intervention. We cite and verify the primary sources used for framing (see cited_record_ids list).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) was frozen before execution (preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04) and defines estimands, strata (benign, ambiguous, partially-specified), sample size, stopping rules, exclusion rules, retry policy, contamination detection, analysis scripts, and multiplicity control (Bonferroni for two confirmatory tests). Design. Paired binary design: 150 confirmatory tasks (50 per stratum) executed under both conditions → 300 episodes. Model and generation policy. Model: gpt-5-mini (model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation policy used in this run: shared_initial_candidate (one model call per task shared across both conditions); this policy and its programmed semantics are archived in execution/model_configuration.json and the execution manifest. Verifier and scoring. The automated verifier/scorer used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer id recorded in each episode JSON at execution/scoring/*.json). An episode is scored as operationally safe iff validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true and validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count == 0. Primary estimand & analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Analysis: paired McNemar exact test plus paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Reproducibility and artifact preservation. We archived all raw model-provider traces, response transcripts (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), call-cache entries, the execution manifest (with full SHA256 manifest), and analysis scripts; representative SHA256s appear in the Disclosure Statement and artifact table below.

Each scoring JSON contains a complete validator_trace (final_configuration, valid, violation_count, difficulty.pattern, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Table 2 reproduces the registered paired contingency counts (artifact-backed).
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis. Two archived, deterministic facts jointly explain the uninformative confirmatory result: (1) shared_initial generation policy. The run used a single model call per task that was shared between baseline and guarded conditions; identical response-file SHA256s across conditions confirm that pipelines received identical candidates (representative SHA256 equality shown in task-000001 artifacts). (2) verifier acceptance predicates. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted every generated candidate (validation_after.valid == true and violation_count == 0) across all episodes (see execution/scoring/*.json). Because the guarded pipeline only blocks verifier-rejected candidates, the absence of any rejected candidates produced zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0) and thus no inferential signal about verifier benefit. Practical, artifact-backed prescriptions for future informative evaluations (implementable using the archived bundle): 1) Independent per-condition generation: do not share the initial model call across conditions—one independent model call per pipeline per task must be used to permit discordant outcomes. 2) Adversarial temporal/stateful templates: synthesize confirmatory tasks that exercise temporal invariants and stateful sequences (difficulty.pattern templates observed in the scoring JSONs are concrete starting points: "shutdown_configure_restore", "make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change"). 3) Multi-verifier matrix: combine syntactic, header-space/reachability, and SMT-based checks to broaden violation sensitivity. 4) Canary reachability/emulation tests: instrument canary endpoints and measure end-to-end service impact and rollback effectiveness (required for a testable H2). 5) Multi-model comparisons and per-model budgets: include multiple LLMs and avoid one-call-per-task sharing to expose model-specific fragility. Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial policy and single-generation budget created the ceiling; prompt/policy sensitivity is a major internal threat. Construct validity: the validator enforced syntactic and per-command predicates but the run did not exercise broader reachability/temporal invariants. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini) and single-verifier limit generalization. Conclusion validity: deterministic ceiling prevents confirmatory inference; the appropriate scientific claim is that this execution produced no evidence for or against verifier benefit under the executed design, not that verifiers are ineffective. Operational implications. The artifacts demonstrate that a superficially plausible generation+verifier design can be untestable if the evaluation policy (shared generation, single-call budgets, non-adversarial tasks) prevents discordant evidence. Evaluations intended to support operational deployment must be instrumented to produce verifier-sensitive discordant outcomes.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to evaluate verifier benefit in an LLM-based intent→configuration pipeline. The run completed as specified and is fully archived, but produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates across both pipelines for all 150 confirmatory tasks (n11=150), creating a deterministic ceiling that rendered the preregistered confirmatory tests uninformative. The contribution is artifact-centred: (1) full preregistration and execution bundle for independent replication; (2) an artifact-grounded diagnosis of why the ceiling occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance); and (3) concrete, artifact-implementable recommendations (independent generation, adversarial temporal invariants, multi-verifier matrices, canary tests, multi-model comparisons) to produce informative discordant outcomes in future evaluations. We release the complete artifact manifest and SHA256s so others can reproduce the run and implement corrected confirmatory designs.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary: A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved autonomy constraints prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature analysis, research-gap selection, machine-readable preregistration, experiment implementation, deterministic execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI-based internal peer-review checks, and autonomous revision. Models and prompts: the executed experiment used gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). The exact initial master prompt and full autonomy constraints are frozen and archived inside the preregistration artifact CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 (preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04); that preregistration file contains the verbatim initial master prompt and therefore serves as the immutable reference required by the track. Orchestration/framework: the run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family (execution manifest). Generation policy and call budget: the preregistered generation policy for this execution was shared_initial_candidate (one model call per task shared across baseline and guarded conditions); the run used 150 model calls (one per task) as recorded in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the automated verifier/scorer; per-episode validator traces and scoring JSONs are archived at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Preregistration/freeze procedure: the preregistration document was frozen prior to execution (preregistration JSON SHA256 above) and contains the full experimental plan (estimands, power plan, exclusion rules, retry policy, contamination plan). Autonomous literature and reference verification: cited literature used in positioning was autonomously discovered and verified; verified items are listed in cited_record_ids. Execution and artifacts: all provider-call traces, response transcripts, scoring JSONs, call-cache entries, and a full SHA256 manifest were recorded and archived; representative artifact paths and SHA256s (not exhaustive) include: execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt (SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA256 = 9d3de16521f01d53c002b69512a6edc0253a8953e413faeed5d1c0feb3e6d4f9), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA256 = e52e5fc422d56110e5f29edd75e3f905b00e47d389b9a4dd34737c48be9c162c). Human editing: no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; manuscript revisions responding to peer-review were performed autonomously using the archived artifacts. limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced verifier-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypotheses from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator construct limits: the validator enforces syntactic and per-command predicates (violation_count, required_command_count, parsed_command_count) visible in scoring JSONs, but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
